brief: Weekly GS Financials & REITs sales color. Financials and REITs outperformed the broader market last week (+1-2%) as it broadened out from tech, led by defensive names (P&C insurance, exchanges, healthcare REITs), consumer-exposed names (payments, lodging and retail REITs) and information services, which diverged from consensus-long software; laggards were cyclical (industrial REITs, banks) and capital markets (alts, investment banks, moneycenters). Fundamental investors were frustrated that price action was macro-driven. Feedback diverged from performance on several names: BLK and BNY got bullish feedback that matched performance, RF outperformed despite bearish feedback, IBKR and C underperformed bullish hopes, and PGR's bearish feedback aligned with its underperformance. For next week's earnings the note runs bull/bear debates by name: BX (alt green-shoot hopes versus datacenter and AI-slowdown concerns plus BREIT/BREP questions), AXP (agentic-commerce cardmember tailwinds versus opex flexibility), NTRS (cautious versus peers on expenses), CBRE (bearish broker-guide fears easing into earnings), WTFC/EWBC/BPOP as rate beneficiaries, FLG/OZK CRE caution, plus FCNCA, FITB, LAZ and MSCI. GS Prime data show Financials net sold (-1.2 SDs, 1-year) on short sales outpacing long buys 4.4-to-1, led by capital markets and insurance, while consumer finance and banks were modestly net bought.
